# Temple Scroll Column 59 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 59 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**59:1** When you enter the land the LORD your God is giving you, do not adopt the disgusting practices of the nations living there.

**59:2** No one among you shall sacrifice a son or daughter in the fire,

**59:3** or practice fortune-telling, interpret omens, cast spells,

**59:4** use charms, consult the dead through a spirit medium, or seek guidance from those who communicate with the dead.

**59:5** Anyone who does these things is detestable to the LORD, and it is because of these very practices that the LORD your God is driving those nations out ahead of you.

**59:6** You must be completely faithful to the LORD your God.

**59:7** The nations you are about to displace consult fortune-tellers and diviners, but the LORD your God does not allow you to do this.

**59:8** Instead, I will raise up a prophet for them from among your own people, one of your own brothers, like you. I will put My words in his mouth, and he will tell the people everything I command.

**59:9** If anyone refuses to listen to the words that prophet speaks on My behalf, I will personally hold that person accountable.

**59:10** But a prophet who dares to speak a message in My name that I have not authorized, or who speaks on behalf of other gods, must be put to death.

**59:11** You may wonder: How will we know if a message has not come from the LORD?

**59:12** If what a prophet says in the LORD's name does not happen or come true, that message did not come from the LORD. The prophet was speaking on his own presumption. Do not be afraid of him.

**59:13** When I destroy the nations whose land I am giving you, and you take over their territory and settle in their towns and houses,

**59:14** you must designate three cities of refuge in the heart of the land I am giving you.

**59:15** Build roads to these cities and divide your territory into three regions, so that anyone who accidentally kills someone may flee there for safety.

**59:16** Here is how the provision works for someone who kills accidentally and flees there to save his life: it applies to anyone who kills a neighbor unintentionally, without any previous hostility —

**59:17** for example, two men go into the forest to cut wood, and as one swings his axe to fell a tree, the axe head flies off the handle and fatally strikes the other man. The survivor may flee to one of these cities and be safe.

**59:18** This is necessary so that the dead man's relative who wants revenge does not chase the killer in a rage and catch up to him because the distance is too great, and kill him — even though the man did not deserve to die, since he had no prior grudge against the victim.

**59:19** That is why I command you: Set apart three cities.

**59:20** If the LORD your God later expands your borders, as He promised your ancestors, and gives you all the land He pledged to them —

**59:21** and if you carefully obey everything I am commanding you today — to love the LORD your God and always follow His ways — then you must add three more cities of refuge to the original three.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Column 59 covers the prohibition of pagan divination (Deut 18:9-14), the prophet-like-Moses promise (18:15-22), and the cities of refuge (19:1-10). The occult practices are translated with modern equivalents for clarity. "Fortune-telling" for qesem, "interpret omens" for me'onen, "cast spells" for menachesh. The cities of refuge are presented as a practical asylum system for accidental death.*
